module.title: Azure deployment and network boundaries
module.summary: Place Cinderline's Entra tenant, subscription, workspace resource, locked managed resource group and both compute planes on Azure, compare the two supported network patterns, keep storage access apart from application access, and diagnose a denied and an unreachable request in order.
objectives: Draw Cinderline's Azure deployment with each resource in the subscription, resource group or account that owns it, and compare the default managed VNet with VNet injection by duty.
Trace one query's author, control, execution and storage paths, separating application access in Unity Catalog from storage access through the access connector's managed identity.
Run ordered diagnoses for a denied and an unreachable request, assemble a permissions and network evidence checklist, and list what differs from AWS.

scenarios.title: Write Cinderline's Azure deployment note for security review
scenarios.context: Fictional Cinderline Components runs dbw-cinderline-prod on the default managed VNet and is adding dbw-cinderline-sec with VNet injection in the same region and Entra tenant. Its sources are the ADLS Gen2 account stcinderlinelake in Cinderline's subscription, a supplier drop account stsupplierdrop in another subscription of the same tenant owned by the supplier-relations team, and an Azure SQL database behind a private endpoint that serverless jobs must reach. Security requires no public IPs on compute, no public network access to either storage account, private user access to dbw-cinderline-sec, no storage keys in any configuration, and named evidence for every boundary. Tier, regional support and preview status are unconfirmed.
scenarios.task: Produce a one-page note for the security specialist: the resources per subscription and resource group, the two network patterns with their duties, the identities and both authorization chains for each storage account, the private connectivity with its DNS zones and approvers, the two diagnostic sequences the operations team will follow, and an explicit list of unknowns and AWS differences.
requirements: Place every resource in the subscription, resource group or Databricks account that owns it, including both managed resource groups.
Give each storage account its application chain and its storage chain separately: principal and privileges; connector identity, data role and network rules.
Name each private endpoint with its sub-resource, network, Private DNS zone and approver.
Separate the denied-request sequence from the unreachable-request sequence, with evidence rows.
Mark tier, region, preview status and charges as unknown until verified; provision nothing.
scenarios.model:
### Resources and planes
Cinderline's Entra tenant trusts `sub-cinderline-data`. `rg-cinderline-data` holds `dbw-cinderline-prod` (default managed VNet), `dbw-cinderline-sec` (VNet injection), the access connector `ac-cinderline-uc` and `stcinderlinelake`; `rg-cinderline-net` holds `vnet-cinderline-data`, the route table, the private endpoints and the Private DNS zones. Each workspace has its own locked managed resource group (workspace storage, cluster VMs; for prod also its VNet, NSG and NAT gateway). `stsupplierdrop` sits in the supplier-relations team's subscription. Control plane and serverless compute run in the Databricks account.

### Patterns and duties
Prod: Databricks operates the network; no routes or endpoints can be added. Sec: host and container subnets delegated to `Microsoft.Databricks/workspaces`, /26 each (59 nodes); `0.0.0.0/0` to the hub firewall plus `AzureDatabricks`, `Storage` and `EventHub` service-tag routes; back-end Private Link once Premium is confirmed.

### Authorization chains
Application chain for every source: Entra sign-in, identities provisioned (automatic identity management, or `sp-job-nightly` added by hand), then `USE CATALOG`, `USE SCHEMA`, `SELECT`. Storage chain: `ac-cinderline-uc`'s managed identity holds Storage Blob Data Reader on the `quality` container; credential `cinderline_lake_cred`; external location `cinderline_quality`. For `stsupplierdrop`, the supplier team assigns the same identity a data role and admits Cinderline through private endpoints only: with public network access disabled, a resource instance rule, which acts on the public endpoint, is not an option. No keys, SAS or client secrets anywhere.

### Private connectivity
Front-end: `databricks_ui_api` and `browser_authentication` endpoints in the transit VNet, `privatelink.azuredatabricks.net` linked to it. Storage: `pe-lake-dfs` (`dfs`) in `snet-pe`, `privatelink.dfs.core.windows.net` linked to `vnet-cinderline-data`. Serverless: NCC `ncc-cinderline` with rules for `stcinderlinelake` (`dfs`) and the SQL database, each approved by its owner.

### Diagnosis
Denied: record the error and who answered; confirm the run-as principal; check catalog privileges; then the connector identity's role; then the storage network rules; rerun as the same principal; write the row. Unreachable: resolve from the asking network; zone links; endpoint state; effective routes; NSG and firewall logs; NCC rule state for serverless; retest from the same place.

### Unknowns and AWS differences
Unknown: Premium confirmation, endpoint support for the SQL resource type in the region, NCC limits, networking charges, the supplier team's approval. Differs from AWS: a locked managed group instead of a workspace configuration, delegated subnets, a managed identity with a role instead of a trust policy, Private DNS zone links. Nothing is provisioned.
scenarios.reasoning: The note keeps Azure's own objects in view (the locked managed groups, delegated subnets, managed identities with roles, Private DNS zone links), keeps the two authorization chains apart so a network fault is never answered with a grant, and turns every conditional feature into a verification item rather than a promise.

disclosures.question: Will the supplier-relations team approve private endpoint requests from Databricks against stsupplierdrop?
disclosures.response: Unknown; they approve endpoint requests only through a change ticket. Until one is approved, stsupplierdrop is marked unreadable from serverless in the design.

disclosures.question: Is dbw-cinderline-sec on the Premium tier?
disclosures.response: The purchase record says Premium, but nobody has confirmed it on the workspace itself; back-end Private Link stays unverified until someone does.

claims.description: The control plane runs in the Azure Databricks account, classic compute in the customer's Azure subscription and serverless compute in the Databricks account; creating a workspace provisions a managed resource group holding its virtual machines, storage accounts and networking components, protected by an Azure deny assignment that blocks changes even when a role grants them.
claims.context: Workspace resource, planes and managed resource group on Azure.

claims.description: SCIM provisioning cannot sync nested groups or Microsoft Entra service principals; automatic identity management syncs users, groups, memberships, nested groups and service principals.
claims.context: Azure Databricks identities from Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.description: VNet injection uses two dedicated subnets delegated to Microsoft.Databricks/workspaces, each node taking one address in each and Azure reserving five per subnet; Databricks manages the required NSG rules through the delegation; with secure cluster connectivity nodes have no public IP and connect outbound to the relay.
An injected workspace needs a user-defined route for every type of outbound connection, and service tags such as AzureDatabricks, Storage and EventHub are recommended over IP addresses.

A Unity Catalog storage credential on Azure names an access connector whose managed identity holds an Azure data role on the storage account; an external location binds an abfss path to it; Shared Key and SAS tokens signed with it authorize the bearer, and disallowing Shared Key rejects them while Entra-authorized requests continue.
claims.context: Unity Catalog storage access on Azure, with the legacy contrast.

claims.description: Azure Databricks Private Link has front-end, back-end and serverless connection types; back-end requires the Premium plan and VNet injection; a name resolves to an endpoint's private address only through a linked Private DNS zone such as privatelink.azuredatabricks.net or privatelink.dfs.core.windows.net, or DNS forwarding.
claims.context: Private connectivity and DNS on Azure.

claims.description: Network connectivity configurations are account-level regional objects attached to workspaces; without a private endpoint serverless reaches Azure storage through service endpoints, and a private endpoint rule is used only after the resource owner approves it.
claims.context: Azure serverless compute plane; availability varies.

concepts.definition: The resource group Azure provisions with a Databricks workspace resource to hold its storage, networking and cluster machines, locked by a system deny assignment.
A user, group, service principal or managed identity in the Entra tenant, synced to Databricks by provisioning and able to hold Azure roles.
Deploying classic compute into two customer subnets delegated to Databricks, whose required NSG rules Databricks manages and whose nodes have no public IP.
The Azure resource whose managed identity Unity Catalog uses to reach a storage account, registered as a storage credential and bound to paths by external locations.

concepts.term: Private Link and Private DNS zone (Azure)
concepts.definition: A private endpoint gives a service a private address in a VNet; a Private DNS zone linked to the asking VNet makes its name resolve there.
An account-level regional object that gives serverless compute stable subnets or owner-approved private endpoints to customer resources.
A denied request reached a control that refused it and names that layer; an unreachable request never arrived and is diagnosed outward from the asking network.
